children: CATL unveiled TECTRANS II, a next‑gen commercial vehicle battery platform, at IAA Transportation 2026 and signed an MoU with DHL Group to co-develop Green Freight Corridors in Europe, building on their 2024 agreement.
New platform targets commercial EV segment, a key growth vector for CATL’s battery sales mix.
MoU with DHL Group in Europe
Partnership could drive deployment volume via DHL’s network, aiding adoption and orders.
Lifecycle economics and durability are critical for fleet TCO, influencing buyer decisions.
Real-world pilots can accelerate OEM uptake and convert to larger contracts if successful.

This is an early-to-mid stage move extending CATL’s push into commercial vehicle electrification with a named logistics partner. For a larger catalyst, look for signed purchase orders, deployment scale, and OEM tie-ups converting pilots into fleet rollouts.
